title: A network of rings reads its genus: two rings of cuts per handle keep one piece
subject: Networks of rings joined by shared contacts, read with the canonical knot test on their space-time law
conclusion: In any network of rule-60 rings with law (12,12) contacts, after any contacts are cut, the pieces read from which uncut contacts need which rings are exactly the components of the ring graph without the cut contacts. So a family of rings of cuts keeps the network in one piece exactly when it is independent in the homology mod 2 of the surface the positions define: at most two per handle keep one piece, some two per handle do, and one more always separates. The torus cut round both ways stays in one piece; the regular genus-2 network of 16 rings with three contacts each keeps every contact persistent and reads its genus the same way.
